cost_correction_note: I1 CORRECTION (2026-09-04, post-hoc): dispatch-fixture.sh's cost/credit figures cited throughout this record were undercounted by a step_finish cost-overwrite bug (fixed in commit 505d35a) that summed only the LAST turn's cost instead of every turn's cost for each multi-step dispatch. Corrected observed_cost/derived_credits for every dispatch with surviving raw.jsonl evidence are recorded in each dispatch.json's cost_correction block and in models/routing/opencode/eval/records/phase-r/budget-ledger.json's i1_correction block. canonical_cost_reference is corrected to false: this record's own inline cost figures predate the fix and are known-undercounted; do not cite them for budget accounting.
i2_correction_note: I2 FINDING (2026-09-04, post-hoc): the clean-control fixture repair (commit a96c0ce) fixed eval/fixtures/reviewer-seeded-defects/clean/{api.sh,pagination.sh} but was never propagated to the case override files cases/R-API/api.sh and cases/R-BOUNDARY/pagination.sh, which still carried the OLD vulnerable patterns the clean-control repair replaced. Independent verification of R-API/dispatch/response.txt and R-BOUNDARY/dispatch/response.txt confirms both cases' 'blocking' findings are entirely about the reintroduced old-pattern vulnerability (JSON-escaping for R-API, arbitrary command execution via array-subscript substitution for R-BOUNDARY) with zero mention of the seeded ground-truth defect (field-rename for R-API, zero-boundary for R-BOUNDARY). 2 of the 5 credited detections in per_id_detections are therefore NOT detections of the seeded defects. This verdict is PENDING_RE_VERIFICATION until cases/R-API and cases/R-BOUNDARY are repaired to preserve only their seeded defect (pending explicit human-authorized fixture repair, the same pattern used for the R-ERROR storage.sh repair) and the affected cases are rerun.
i2_rerun_note:
I2 REPAIR RERUN (2026-09-04): R-API and R-BOUNDARY were redispatched live against the properly repaired fixture (case files now preserve only their seeded defect; see fixtures-test.sh regression tests). Prior mis-attributed evidence archived at eval/records/phase-r/reviewer/pre-i2-fix/. 

Result is NOT 5/5. New findings: 
(1) R-API: the model reported ZERO findings against api.sh in this dispatch -- the seeded defect (documented displayName field silently renamed to name) received no signal at all, not even as a suggestion. This differs from the prior run's problem (wrong vulnerability flagged); here nothing was flagged for the seeded defect. Single-sample model-judgment outcome, not yet root-caused.
(2) R-BOUNDARY: credited 'material' by the mechanical scorer (a material/blocking finding was reported against pagination.sh, the case's override file), but the finding is NOT about the seeded zero-boundary defect -- it is about leading-zero octal misinterpretation in bash arithmetic ( (( "0144" )) evaluates as octal 144 = decimal 100, bypassing the intended 1..100 bound; (( "08" )) is an invalid octal digit and raises a bash arithmetic error rather than a clean rejection). This is a genuine, previously-undiscovered defect in the numeric-format guard ( [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] ) that clean/pagination.sh has carried since the original clean-control repair (commit a96c0ce) and that this session's I2 fix (commit 5d157e7) propagated verbatim into cases/R-BOUNDARY/pagination.sh. It is present in EVERY case sandbox's copy of pagination.sh (all 6 sandboxes include clean/pagination.sh), not only R-BOUNDARY's. The clean control's own dispatch did not flag it (0 material findings recorded there), which is model-response variance across dispatches against the same file content, not evidence the bug is absent.

No further fixture modification, rerun, or effort escalation was made after this rerun -- both findings above require explicit human authorization before any further change, per this plan's established fixture-touch pattern.
